source.title: The topology of molecular representations and its influence on machine learning performance
source.authors: Florian Rottach; Sebastian Schieferdecker; Carsten Eickhoff

record.file_problem: none; full article text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether topological properties of molecular representations predict model test error, extending generalization-measure analysis to molecular regression tasks. It does not test the claim versions listed.
record.gate_note: The study reports correlations between molecular representation topology and model test errors, plus cross-validation results for TopoLearn. It does not test random-label memorization, image convolutional versus fully connected networks, optimizer or batch effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study measures molecular feature-space topology and predicts held-out regression error. None of its results tests V1–V8. In particular, representation topology is not magnitude-aware weight sharpness, and test error is not the training–test error gap. Width and batch size appear only in hyperparameter searches, without results isolating their effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the conclusion: persistent-homology features predict relative molecular test error, and TopoLearn outperforms the evaluated modelability measures in two cross-validation schemes. The authors associate effective representations with more input features and shorter persistence lifetimes. Higher input dimensionality should be distinguished from higher estimated persistent-homology dimension, which they associate with greater error. They also acknowledge that topology alone cannot fully explain performance and that label alignment matters.
record.recipe_differences: Uses topological descriptors of molecular feature spaces and regression models to predict normalized test error; it does not reproduce the claim's random-label or architecture, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, sharpness, or memorization-removal experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by dataset, representation type, sample size, data split, and distance metric. The authors report lower correlations for solubility and lipophilicity data and note that distance metrics substantially alter topological features.

fits_no_version.finding: Persistent-homology descriptors correlate with molecular regression errors, and TopoLearn predicts relative test RMSE across held-out datasets and representations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Molecular feature-space topology provides information about relative test error, with predictive strength depending on dataset, representation, and splitting strategy.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger subsamples generally yield higher test R2 under random and scaffold splitting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing training-data availability improves held-out molecular regression performance in the evaluated settings.

record.problems: The study uses normalized errors, which the authors say remove information about the spread of the error distribution. Results depend on the selected distance metric. The text reports large variance across datasets and weaker correlations for some datasets and representation types. The evaluated outcomes do not measure train-test error gaps or arbitrary-label memorization.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results were left out. Tables 6, 7, 10, and 11 give separate cross-validation results by representation type and split; the extracted rows retain the overall random-split correlations and the text-stated sample-size and descriptor-correlation findings rather than transcribing every subgroup value.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe. The random-label discussion supplies no such experiment.
Test error as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, including tuning and optimizer modifications.
Batch-size effects under matched epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects, underfitting, and interactions with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness versus training–test error gaps and competing norm or margin measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many randomly selected examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any version, but no version qualifies for a verdict. States marked cannot_determine indicate that the rows do not measure the listed effects; they do not indicate evidence that those effects are absent.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks on image datasets.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning or optimizer changes.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: TopoLearn (PH)
rows.operation_detail: Cross-validated prediction of normalized test RMSE from persistent homology descriptors; reported correlation with actual model errors.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation between predicted and actual normalized test error
rows.locator: Results, Predicting generalization with TopoLearn; Table 6
rows.note: The text reports an average correlation across evaluated datasets; it does not provide a train-test error gap.
rows.check: Reports the study's own prediction method's performance, not a claim-version effect. Table 6 gives mean fold correlation 0.62 ± 0.18 and pooled correlation 0.63 for random-split LODO evaluation. Its LORO caption conflicts with the surrounding text. The prose incorrectly extends 0.62 to both splits; scaffold LODO is 0.47 ± 0.24 in Table 10.

source_check.correct: Mean fold correlation: 0.62 ± 0.18; aggregated correlation: 0.63; random-split LODO evaluation. The constructed TopoLearn dataset has 2550 samples and 66 features; TopoLearn (PH) uses only persistent-homology descriptors, whose input count is not separately stated.
